comparisons.peer_summary: Under the 2017 Plan, eligible employees can withhold up to 15% of earnings to purchase shares at 85% of the lower of fair market value on the first or last day of a six-month offering period commencing in May and November.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) that allows employees to purchase stock at an 85% discount based on a look-back period of fair market value. A key similarity is the withholding limit: both caps eligible earnings withholding at 15% (NVIDIA: "up to 15% of their earnings withheld"; AMD: "up to 15% of their eligible earnings withheld"). A difference exists in the offering period structure: NVIDIA describes a 24-month offering divided into four six-month purchase periods, whereas AMD specifies six-month offering periods commencing in May and November without mentioning a multi-year container structure.

sentences.text: Employees who participate in the 2012 Plan may have up to 15% of their earnings withheld to purchase shares of common stock.

The price of common stock purchased under our 2012 Plan will be equal to 85% of the lower of the fair market value of the common stock on the commencement date of each offering period or the fair market value of the common stock on each purchase date within the offering.

Under the 2017 Plan, eligible employees who participate in an offering period may have up to 15% of their eligible earnings withheld, up to certain limitations, to purchase shares of common stock at 85% of the lower of the fair market value on the first or the last business day of the six-month offering period.
The offering periods commence in May and November each year.

comparisons.peer_topic: Employee Stock Purchase Plan Structure and Terms
comparisons.peer_summary: The ESPP allows eligible employees to acquire common stock via payroll deductions at 85% of the fair market value using a 6-month look-back period, and is structured as a qualified plan under Section 423 of the Internal Revenue Code but not as a qualified pension or ERISA plan.
comparisons.comparison: Broadcom and NVIDIA both offer an ESPP providing a 15% discount (85% of fair market value) using a look-back mechanism comparing the start and end of an offering period. NVIDIA uses a 24-month offering period with six-month purchase windows, while Broadcom uses a 6-month look-back period structure. Both utilize payroll deductions (NVIDIA: "withheld"; Broadcom: "periodic payroll deductions") to facilitate these purchases.

sentences.text: The price of common stock purchased under our 2012 Plan will be equal to 85% of the lower of the fair market value of the common stock on the commencement date of each offering period or the fair market value of the common stock on each purchase date within the offering.
Employees who participate in the 2012 Plan may have up to 15% of their earnings withheld to purchase shares of common stock.

The ESPP provides eligible employees with the opportunity to acquire an ownership interest in us through periodic payroll deductions, based on a 6-month look-back period, at a price equal to the lesser of 85% of the fair market value of our common stock at either the beginning or the end of the relevant offering period.

comparisons.peer_summary: The 2006 Employee Stock Purchase Plan allows eligible employees to buy common stock at 85% of its value on specific dates. As of December 28, 2024, 118 million shares remained available for issuance out of 523 million authorized shares through August 2026.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both provide an ESPP with a purchase price set at 85% of the fair market value. A specific difference lies in the disclosure of withholding mechanics: NVIDIA explicitly defines a participation cap, stating employees may have "up to 15% of their earnings withheld," whereas Intel's cited text confirms the 85% pricing but does not specify the maximum withholding percentage in the provided sentences, only noting share availability.

comparisons.peer_topic: ESPP Contribution Limits and Purchase Price Mechanics
comparisons.peer_summary: The ESPP allows substantially all employees to purchase common stock via payroll deductions up to 15% of eligible compensation, with a purchase price equal to 85% of the lower of the fair market value on the first or last day of the six-month offering period.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and NVIDIA share identical mechanics for their ESPP discount and contribution limits. Both companies set the purchase price at "85% of the lower of the fair market value" on the first and last days of the offering period. Both also cap employee contributions at "up to 15%" of eligible compensation/earnings. A similarity is the use of payroll deductions/withholding.

sentences.text: The price of common stock purchased under our 2012 Plan will be equal to 85% of the lower of the fair market value of the common stock on the commencement date of each offering period or the fair market value of the common stock on each purchase date within the offering.
Employees who participate in the 2012 Plan may have up to 15% of their earnings withheld to purchase shares of common stock.

Our ESPP is offered to substantially all employees and permitted eligible employees to purchase shares of our common stock through payroll deductions of up to 15% of their eligible compensation, subject to certain limitations.
The purchase price of the shares under the ESPP equals 85% of the lower of the fair market value of our common stock on either the first or last day of each six-month offering period.
